_format.description: Ujednolicony format eksportu danych ze stron NASA (science.nasa.gov i pokrewnych). Ten sam schemat stosuj do każdej kolejnej strony misji/pojazdu, aby wszystkie wpisy były spójne i mogły być łączone w jedną bazę.
conventions: Klucze zawsze obecne; brak danych = null (nigdy nie usuwaj klucza), brak pozycji = pusta lista [].
Daty: 'date' zawsze w ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD), 'date_raw' zachowuje oryginalny zapis ze strony.
Wszystkie URL-e bezwzględne (https://...), bez parametrów śledzących gdzie to możliwe.
Każdy zasób medialny jest obiektem z minimalnym zestawem pól: url + typ + context (skąd pochodzi na stronie).
Treść artykułu w polach 'markdown': nagłówki '##'/'###', listy '-', listy numerowane '1.', pogrubienia '**'. Układ = kolejność sekcji ze strony źródłowej.
Treść zachowywana w języku źródła (pole source.language); nie tłumaczyć przy ekstrakcji.
Pola 'id' zewnętrznych systemów (np. PIA##### z Photojournal, identyfikatory YouTube, numery modeli 3D) zapisuj w dedykowanych polach *_id, jeśli są znane.
Weryfikuj dostępność URL-i (HTTP 200) przed zapisem; martwy link oznaczaj w polu 'status'.

article.title: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter
article.lead: NASA's Ingenuity Mars Helicopter completed 72 historic flights since first taking to the skies above the Red Planet.

sections.heading: 5 Years Since Ingenuity's 'Wright Brothers Moment'
sections.markdown:
After riding to Mars strapped beneath the Perseverance rover, the Ingenuity helicopter took to the Martian air for its initial flight on April 19, 2021 — the first powered flight on another planet.

[Learn the Story Behind Ingenuity](https://youtu.be/qwdfdE6ruMw)

sections.heading: The Legacy of Ingenuity (Featured Video)
sections.markdown:
On April 19, 2021, NASA's Ingenuity Mars Helicopter made history when it completed the first powered, controlled flight on the Red Planet. It flew for the last time on Jan. 18, 2024.

Designed to be a technology demonstration that would make no more than five test flights in 30 days, the helicopter eventually completed 72 flights across nearly three years, soaring higher and faster than previously imagined. Ingenuity embarked on a new mission as an operations demonstration, serving as an aerial scout for scientists and rover planners, and for engineers ready to learn more about Perseverance's landing-gear debris.

In its final phase, the helicopter entered a new engineering demonstration phase where it executed experimental flight tests that further expanded the team's knowledge of the vehicle's aerodynamic limits.

**Film:** [Legacy of NASA's Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (YouTube)](https://youtu.be/qMbHE_VXI-8)

sections.heading: Key Facts
sections.markdown:
- **Launch:** July 30, 2020, Cape Canaveral Air Force Station, Florida
- **Landed:** Feb. 18, 2021, Jezero Crater, Mars
- **Length of mission:** Technology demonstration completed; transitioned to new [operations demo](https://science.nasa.gov/missions/mars-2020-perseverance/nasas-ingenuity-helicopter-to-begin-new-demonstration-phase/) phase. [Mission completed](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/after-three-years-on-mars-nasas-ingenuity-helicopter-mission-ends/) on Jan. 25, 2024.

sections.heading: 5 Things to Know
sections.markdown:
1. The first aircraft to achieve powered, controlled flight on another planet, a feat that's been called a "Wright Brothers moment."
2. Completed 128.8 flying minutes, covering 10.5 miles (17.0 kilometers), and reaching altitudes as high as 78.7 feet (24.0 meters).
3. Successfully flying in the extremely thin Martian atmosphere.
4. Previewing areas of Mars of possible interest for the Perseverance rover to explore.
5. Paved the way for future aerial explorers at Mars and, potentially, other space destinations.

sections.heading: Tech Specs
sections.markdown:
- **Mass:** 3.97 pounds (1.8 kilograms)
- **Weight:** 4 pounds on Earth (1.81 kilograms on Mars); 1.5 pounds on Mars (0.68 kilograms)
- **Width:** Total length of rotors: Approximately 4 feet (approximately 1.2 meters) tip to tip
- **Power:** Solar panel charges Lithium-ion batteries, providing enough energy for one 90-second flight per Martian day (approximately 350 Watts of average power during flight)
- **Blade span:** Just under 4 feet (1.2 meters)
- **Flight range:** Up to 980 feet (300 meters)
- **Flight altitude:** Up to 15 feet (5 meters)
- **Flight environment:** Thin atmosphere, less than 1 percent as dense as Earth's

sections.heading: The Next Generation: NASA's SkyFall Mars Helicopters
sections.markdown:
NASA's SkyFall mission will build on the success of the Ingenuity Mars helicopter, which achieved the first powered, controlled flight on another planet. Using a daring mid-air deployment, SkyFall will deliver a team of next-gen Mars helicopters to scout human landing sites and map subsurface water ice. The mission was announced as part of the agency's "Ignition" event on Tuesday, March 24.

[Learn More About SkyFall](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/skyfall/) — [film na YouTube](https://youtu.be/TYasUWRkv4E)

sections.markdown:

sections.heading: Ingenuity Posters
sections.markdown:
Download high-resolution posters to celebrate Ingenuity's accomplishments.

- **Ingenuity: 72 Pathbreaking Flights** — Ingenuity flew for the last time on January 18, 2024, and completed its mission on January 25, 2024, after nearly three years of aerial exploration and 72 historic flights. [Download Poster](https://science.nasa.gov/resource/ingenuity-72-pathbreaking-flights-poster/)
- **Ingenuity Mars Helicopter Poster** — Celebrate the accomplishments of NASA's Ingenuity Mars Helicopter with a vertical or horizontal poster illustration depicting the first helicopter on the Red Planet. [Download Poster](https://science.nasa.gov/resource/ingenuity-mars-helicopter-poster/)
- **Ingenuity Mars Helicopter By the Numbers** — In the more than two years since landing, the helicopter has greatly exceeded its planned lifespan and evolved from a test of the first powered, controlled flight on another world to working to support other goals. [Download Infographic](https://science.nasa.gov/resource/ingenuity-mars-helicopter-by-the-numbers/)
